correctness.rationale: For F in {T,S,TS}, sum N=1 and N=2 histories exactly. Their first-order rates are (1/2,1,2 E Q²); every N>=3 contribution is O_B(lambda²), using Poisson(lambda B) total-progeny domination and bounded T<=S<=BN. Therefore covariance expansion holds with all quantifiers and boundary cases. Exact finite-support checks agree, but are not the proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2014 theorem computes separate expectations of extinction time and total lifetime, not the mixed moment or distribution-sensitive first derivative. The 2013 predecessor states mean occupation-time identities. The 2018 memoryless branching study is in a different lifetime class and parameter regime. Existing nearby published covariance findings concern stationary delay systems, generic stopping moments, or renewal residual lives and do not imply the small-birth age-dependent branching law. Full-text and semantic comparisons support originality, without excluding an unindexed equivalent.
